details: This package republishes the Baileys WhatsApp Web library under the @ikyybella scope with the upstream name intact and adds a hidden installer-independent action to it. lib/Socket/newsletter.js contains an injected, unguarded 90-second setTimeout inside the newsletter socket factory that fires on every connection and issues a WhatsApp "w:mex" query with QueryIds.FOLLOW against the hardcoded channel JID 120363425000320171@newsletter — silently subscribing the linked WhatsApp account to that channel, with errors swallowed and no API call or user consent. lib/Socket/luxu.js additionally hardcodes forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo channel JIDs (120363421563597486@newsletter, 120363399602691477@newsletter) and the channel name "Ikyy" onto outgoing eventMessage and poll messages, so messages sent through this fork inherit forced channel attribution. The package declares a dependency on cache-manager ^7.2.8, a version range that resolves to a release of that otherwise-legitimate caching library which has been separately identified as malicious, so installing this package alongside those libraries pulls the compromised build into the dependency tree. The preinstall hook engine-requirements.js only checks the Node.js major version. The fork contains no credential, token,.npmrc or environment-variable reads and no file exfiltration; all hardcoded network destinations are web[.]whatsapp[.]com, call[.]whatsapp[.]com, wa[.]me and raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com.
